param.name: aoi
param.dialogReference: Required polygon feature layer. The source must have a defined coordinate system. Empty, invalid, non-polygon, or unknown-coordinate-system input is rejected. Geometry is transformed to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326).

param.name: network_dataset
param.dialogReference: Required Network Analyst network dataset. The tool reads but does not modify the source. The selected travel mode and its active restrictions determine traversable edge directions.

param.name: output_folder
param.dialogReference: Required destination folder. The run creates a fingerprinted subfolder containing staged GeoParquet parts, a run manifest, and resumable run state.

param.name: h3_resolution
param.dialogReference: Required integer from 0 through 15. Determines the canonical H3 cells evaluated.

param.name: travel_mode
param.dialogReference: Required travel mode available in the selected network. Edge direction and restriction eligibility are evaluated for this mode.

param.name: snap_tolerance_m
param.dialogReference: Required non-negative maximum geodesic distance, in meters, from a proposed representative to its eligible edge. The default comes from spatial.representative_snap_tolerance_m in config/config.yml (100 meters in the shipped configuration). Network Analyst location distance is also validated in meters.

param.name: batch_size
param.dialogReference: Optional positive integer override. If omitted or left at the inferred suggestion, policy version 1 recommends 100 candidates per GiB of available physical memory, bounded to 100 through 2,000 and to the AOI candidate-cell count.

param.name: part_row_limit
param.dialogReference: Optional positive integer override. If omitted or left at the inferred suggestion, policy version 1 recommends 1,000 rows per 128 MiB of available physical memory, bounded to 500 through 50,000.

param.name: total_output_hard_cap
param.dialogReference: Optional positive integer override. If omitted or left at the inferred suggestion, policy version 1 recommends half of the output volume free bytes divided by 8 KiB per cell, bounded to 1 through 5,000,000. Exceeding the resolved cap fails the run incomplete; output is never silently truncated.

param.name: export_review_feature_class
param.displayname: Also Save Hexagons as Feature Class
param.dialogReference: Optional checkbox, unchecked by default. When checked, after the eligibility run completes the tool also writes a WGS 84 polygon feature class with one H3 hexagon per evaluated cell for interactive review. The GeoParquet output is unchanged.

param.name: review_feature_class
param.dialogReference: Output feature class path, required and enabled only when Also Save Hexagons as Feature Class is checked. It must be in a file, mobile, or enterprise geodatabase. An existing feature class is replaced only when overwrite is enabled. Fields: h3_index (Text 20, the exact decimal integer H3 index equal to GeoParquet h3_id; stored as text because ArcGIS Big Integer fields are limited to 53 bits) and eligibility_status (Text 32). This is a non-published review aid, not a contract artifact.

dataIdInfo.idPurp: Identify H3 cells supported by traversable network edges within a polygon area of interest and write an audited eligibility dataset, optionally exporting H3 hexagons to a feature class for interactive review.
dataIdInfo.idAbs: This tool validates the area of interest and network geometry, identifies eligible H3 cells, and writes audited GeoParquet in WGS 84 (EPSG:4326). It does not solve origin-destination routes. Parameters are aoi, network_dataset, output_folder, h3_resolution, travel_mode, snap_tolerance_m, batch_size, part_row_limit, total_output_hard_cap, export_review_feature_class, and review_feature_class. When export_review_feature_class is checked, the completed run is also exported to review_feature_class as WGS 84 H3 hexagon polygons with h3_index (Text 20, exact decimal integer equal to h3_id) and eligibility_status (Text 32) fields in a geodatabase; this non-published review aid is not part of the data contract. ArcPy selects and logs the highest-ranked available datum transformation for each source extent and fails if none is available. When execution limits are omitted, policy version 1 infers them from available physical memory and output-volume free space. Each effective execution limit is logged as inferred or set and recorded in the manifest with the policy version and resource snapshot. Resumed runs restore the saved values from the manifest rather than probing current resources again. Exceeding the total output hard cap fails the run incomplete; output is never silently truncated. A resource-probe failure is explicit; there is no undocumented fallback.
